Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Is today's Quran the same as the Prophet's?

The Quran was kept by memory, teachers and writing. Tradition, historians, and where they disagree.

Part 1 of 3

﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَـٰفِظُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, it is We who sent down the message [i.e., the Qur’ān], and indeed, We will be its guardian.

Quran · Al-Hijr 15:9

﴿لَّا يَأْتِيهِ ٱلْبَـٰطِلُ مِنۢ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِۦ ۖ تَنزِيلٌ مِّنْ حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; [it is] a revelation from a [Lord who is] Wise and Praiseworthy.

Quran · Fussilat 41:42

Start with what the book says about itself, and be clear about its standing. It says God sent down the Reminder and will guard it, and that falsehood has no way in from before or behind. That is the Quran's own claim. For a reader who already trusts it, it is a promise. For anyone else it is not evidence yet, because a book cannot vouch for itself. So the useful question is what history can add.

A question for you

How should a claim a book makes about itself be treated?

If you sayAs a promise, if I already trust the book.
ThenThat is how a believing reader holds it, and it is a coherent way. This Step shows what history adds beside it.
If you sayAs a claim to be checked against evidence.
ThenThen the next parts are for you: they set out what can be checked, and what cannot.
If you sayAs no evidence at all.
ThenA fair way to treat a self-description. The rest of this Step does not rely on the verse.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَإِذَا قُرِئَ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ فَٱسْتَمِعُوا۟ لَهُۥ وَأَنصِتُوا۟ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

So when the Qur’ān is recited, then listen to it and pay attention that you may receive mercy.

Quran · Al-A'raf 7:204

﴿أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Or add to it, and recite the Qur’ān with measured recitation.

Quran · Al-Muzzammil 73:4

Translation

Only be strong and very courageous. Be careful to observe to do according to all the law which Moses my servant commanded you. Don’t turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may have good success wherever you go. This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success. Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.”

Original · Hebrew

רַק֩ חֲזַ֨ק וֶֽאֱמַ֜ץ מְאֹ֗ד לִשְׁמֹ֤ר לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ כְּכָל־הַתּוֹרָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוְּךָ֙ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדִּ֔י אַל־תָּס֥וּר מִמֶּ֖נּוּ יָמִ֣ין וּשְׂמֹ֑אול לְמַ֣עַן תַּשְׂכִּ֔יל בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּלֵֽךְ׃ לֹֽא־יָמ֡וּשׁ סֵפֶר֩ הַתּוֹרָ֨ה הַזֶּ֜ה מִפִּ֗יךָ וְהָגִ֤יתָ בּוֹ֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה לְמַ֨עַן֙ תִּשְׁמֹ֣ר לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת כְּכָל־הַכָּת֖וּב בּ֑וֹ כִּי־אָ֛ז תַּצְלִ֥יחַ אֶת־דְּרָכֶ֖ךָ וְאָ֥ז תַּשְׂכִּֽיל׃ הֲל֤וֹא צִוִּיתִ֨יךָ֙ חֲזַ֣ק וֶאֱמָ֔ץ אַֽל־תַּעֲרֹ֖ץ וְאַל־תֵּחָ֑ת כִּ֤י עִמְּךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּלֵֽךְ׃

Joshua · 1:7-9

World English Bible

The Quran was a book heard before it was a book read. Verses in it speak of reciting, of listening, of reading aloud with care. So the first way of keeping it was the mouth and the ear: one person recites, another repeats, and the first listens for slips. The practice still exists. A student recites to a teacher, and a teacher who is satisfied may give a certificate naming the line of teachers behind him.

A question for you

What does a chain of teachers give a text that a printed copy cannot?

If you sayA living check: a person who can hear a slip.
ThenThat is how the recitation tradition works: the teacher is the check.
If you sayA link to a person, not only a page.
ThenA fair thing to notice. It is also why the chains are named in the certificates.
If you sayNothing: a chain can drift too.
ThenThat is the honest objection, and the tradition itself recorded differences. The next part is how it responded.

Part 3 of 3

﴿لَا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِۦ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِۦٓ١٦ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا جَمْعَهُۥ وَقُرْءَانَهُۥ١٧ فَإِذَا قَرَأْنَـٰهُ فَٱتَّبِعْ قُرْءَانَهُۥ١٨ ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا بَيَانَهُۥ١٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

Move not your tongue with it, [O Muḥammad], to hasten with it [i.e., recitation of the Qur’ān]. Indeed, upon Us is its collection [in your heart] and [to make possible] its recitation. So when We have recited it [through Gabriel], then follow its recitation. Then upon Us is its clarification [to you].

Quran · Al-Qiyamah 75:16-19

The verse says its collection rests with God. The tradition adds a human side: memory alone can drift. It records that when soldiers from different regions were heard reciting differently, Uthman had copies prepared from the sheets kept by Hafsa and sent to the provinces. That is what the tradition records, in a report told in more than one version. Historians then ask when the written text was finished. Their answers differ, and the manuscripts leave little room for a date much after about 700.

A question for you

When memory and writing disagree on a detail, which do you check first?

If you sayThe person who learned it from the best teacher.
ThenThat is how the recitation tradition works, and the next Step takes it up.
If you sayThe earliest written copy.
ThenThat is how manuscript scholars work, and the next Step looks at the earliest copies.
If you sayBoth, and the places where they differ.
ThenThat is the method of the scholars who study this, and the one this app follows.

The same in the other books

the Gospel (Luke) · 6:12

World English Bible

the Gospel (Mark) · 1:35

World English Bible

Your reflection

What is something you know only because someone taught it to you aloud? Who was it, and what would be lost if only the written page remained?
